newsitem.title: USA: Clinton unveils U.S. economic plan for Africa.
newsitem.headline: Clinton unveils U.S. economic plan for Africa.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday announced a trade and economic development plan for Africa that includes reducing tariffs for counties reforming their economies.

"This is a moment of tremendous promise for the people of Africa," Clinton said, announcing a strategy that includes bi-partisan efforts in Congress to enact legislation to back economic growth on the continent.

The White House said Clinton also would use this week's summit in Denver of the seven leading industrialised nations to seek a coordinated international effort -- including urging the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund to provide debt relief for poor countries.

Under the Clinton plan, the poorest countries in Africa would receive duty-free access for some 1,800 additional products, while any nation "undertaking concerted reforms" for their economies would benefit from reduced tariffs.

Administration officials said some 30 countries in Africa grew at more than five percent last year and a few at around 10 percent. The IMF forecasts 4.7 percent growth for Africa as a whole this year.

The World Bank says that 37 out of 48 sub-Saharan African countries are undertaking serious economic reforms, including liberalising trade barriers, privatising state enterprises and easing investment laws.
